# Analyze historical yellowtail catches by class and DOY to confirm peak windows
import pandas as pd

trips = tables['trips']

# Group by class and DOY to see seasonal patterns
by_class_doy = trips.groupby(['cls', 'fished_date_doy']).agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum',
    'boat': 'count'
}).reset_index()

# Focus on key months: April (DOY 90-120), October (DOY 280-310)
april_data = by_class_doy[(by_class_doy['fished_date_doy'] >= 90) & (by_class_doy['fished_date_doy'] <= 120)]
october_data = by_class_doy[(by_class_doy['fished_date_doy'] >= 280) & (by_class_doy['fished_date_doy'] <= 310)]

print("APRIL PEAK (DOY 90-120):")
print(april_data.sort_values('yt', ascending=False).head(15))
print("\n" + "="*80 + "\n")
print("OCTOBER PEAK (DOY 280-310):")
print(october_data.sort_values('yt', ascending=False).head(15))

# Calculate avg yt per angler by class across the whole year
class_stats = trips.groupby('cls').agg({
    'yt': ['sum', 'mean', 'count'],
    'anglers': 'sum'
}).round(2)
class_stats.columns = ['total_yt', 'mean_yt', 'trips', 'total_anglers']
class_stats['yt_per_angler'] = (class_stats['total_yt'] / class_stats['total_anglers']).round(3)

print("\n" + "="*80 + "\n")
print("CLASS EFFECTIVENESS (all time):")
print(class_stats.sort_values('yt_per_angler', ascending=False))

result = "Analysis complete"

]
sched_now = sched_now[(sched_now['cls'] == 'day_1_5') | (sched_now['cls'] == 'overnight')]
print(sched_now[['boat', 'cls', 'fish_date_doy']].sort_values('fish_date_doy'))

print("\n" + "="*80 + "\n")

# Also check what boats typically run day_1_5 in October (DOY 287-303)
